record.title: Apple preprint reports generalist-model control across simulated and real robot-manipulation tasks
record.summary: The Nov 6 Apple-affiliated preprint introduces AMP1, a reusable harness in which a generalist model observes a robot and directly writes and executes code to control its manipulator as a task unfolds. The authors report 85.6% success on RoboLab-120 with Gemini 4 Argon and 82.8% with Claude Opus 5.5, compared with listed specialist baselines of 49.2% and 42.9%. They also report 104 successes in 108 physical trials across 12 tasks and three Franka Research 3 robots using Opus 5.5 at high reasoning effort. These are paper-reported results, not independent reproductions. The paper reports that AMP1 is slow because much of each episode waits for model reasoning; model/API cost and physical-trial artifacts remain open.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record identifies the paper On Agentic Manipulation Policies as submitted on November 6, 2026, and exposes its full text and supplementary sections.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that AMP1 achieves 85.6% success on RoboLab-120 with Gemini 4 Argon and 82.8% with Claude Opus 5.5, compared with listed leading VLA and WAM results of 49.2% and 42.9%; these are author-run results and were not independently reproduced here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report 104 successes in 108 real-world trials across twelve tasks and three Franka Research 3 instances using Opus 5.5 at high reasoning effort; scripts and raw trial data were not independently inspected in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that persistent memory improves success on RoboDojo bimanual tasks and reduces model calls, and that object/verifier artifacts account for a substantial share of RoboLab failures; these analyses remain author-reported.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected paper does not establish broad real-world generalization, production reliability, competitive latency, total inference cost, or independent replication across labs and hardware.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of RoboLab-120, CaP-Gym, memory results or the 108 physical trials was performed.
Physical-trial raw data, complete per-trial records, and scripts were not independently inspected in this activation.
The paper identifies slow model reasoning but does not provide a complete matched latency and monetary-cost comparison in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported results hold, a generalist model directly controlling robots through a reusable feedback harness could alter robotics-control architecture and reduce dependence on task-specific demonstrations. Consequence is notable but bounded by a single paper, named models, benchmark and robot regime.
limitations: All benchmark and physical-trial outcomes in this record are paper-reported and not independently reproduced by the research desk.
Physical evidence is 108 trials across twelve tasks and three Franka Research 3 instances; it does not establish general deployment performance or reliability across robot types and environments.
The paper reports that AMP1 is not yet practical because a robot spends much of each episode waiting for model reasoning; complete task latency and monetary costs were not established here.
The authors report benchmark object and verifier artifacts and analyze failures; the degree to which these affect cross-paper comparisons remains an evaluation caveat.
The Apple implementation license is custom and third-party benchmark assets have separate terms; this activation did not adopt or execute the code.

relationships.summary: Both papers report RoboLab-120 results, but ZAP studies a specialist policy trained through simulation while AMP1 keeps a generalist model in the control loop; shared benchmark overlap does not make them the same development.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports 85.6% RoboLab-120 success with Gemini 4 Argon, 82.8% with Opus 5.5, and 104/108 physical-trial successes with Opus 5.5 across twelve tasks on three robot instances. It also reports 4.6x lower failure on a memory-augmented RoboDojo evaluation after practice and about 35% fewer model calls.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not fully measured in the reviewed paper. It reports model-call counts for selected ablations, but not a complete matched monetary or latency accounting for the physical trials.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint and its reported study are publicly inspectable. the research desk did not run the harness, reproduce benchmark figures or inspect physical-trial raw records; all outcome numbers remain author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: Research prototype and benchmark/physical-trial study reported in a preprint; broad deployment and operational reliability are not established.
technical.mechanism: AMP1 gives a generalist model visual observations, code execution and direct motion control, keeping the model in the loop so it can revise actions as interactions unfold. A persistent memory variant stores observations, strategies and code across episodes while leaving model weights fixed.
technical.novelty: The paper studies agentic manipulation policies in which a generalist model directly controls a manipulator in a feedback loop rather than selecting only predefined skills or generating a one-shot program.
technical.regime: Author-run evaluation in RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym simulations, plus twelve real-world task types across three Franka Research 3 robots. Main reported models include Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5. The paper notes long per-episode reasoning waits and model/harness/sensing sensitivity.
technical.reproducibility: The paper links implementation/materials, but this activation did not pin the repository, inspect all license terms, run code or independently reproduce results. Physical-trial raw trajectories and scripts remain unverified.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares AMP1 with listed VLA and WAM policies on RoboLab-120 and reports 49.2% and 42.9% respectively; settings are paper-specific and were not independently matched here. On physical trials it reports 49/108 for FLUX 3 Action and 30/108 for pi0.5.

brief.title: Apple preprint reports generalist-model control across simulated and real robot-manipulation tasks
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported results hold in their stated regimes, a generalist model acting directly in a feedback loop could change robotics-control choices and reduce dependence on task-specific demonstrations or prebuilt skills. The evidence is a single paper and a bounded set of tasks, hardware and models; it does not establish broad deployment, low latency or economic viability.

related.summary: Both papers report RoboLab-120 results, but ZAP studies a specialist policy trained through simulation while AMP1 keeps a generalist model in the control loop; shared benchmark overlap does not make them the same development.

other.title: A simulation-trained robot agent reports transfer to new real tasks and a second embodiment
other.summary: A Luma-affiliated arXiv preprint introduces ZAP, which starts from a 27B vision-language model and teaches robot motion through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning entirely in simulation. The authors report 96.7% success over 30 real-robot trials across 10 tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in their harness, with lower average time and cost; the same checkpoint also reports transfer from a bimanual robot to a single-arm Franka. These results are author-reported measurements from a bounded evaluation and have not been independently reproduced.
